items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section III, List of Answers on Topics 19:1
items.html: It is known that every renewal of form is regarded as an addition to the first form. Therefore, if phase four in Malchut was refined into phase three, this is another Malchut that has been added to the first, for there is no absence in spirituality. However, the force of the restriction that is in the Malchut of phase four rides upon the new Malchut of phase three as well, and therefore a coupling by striking applies in her. Even so, she is not regarded as the concluding Malchut, as is the Malchut of phase four in the upper one, before the direct light is clothed in her reflected light — that is, only after she broadens of herself and within herself into ten Sefirot of the Guf, and the reflected light descends to them from above downward together with the whole measure of level that it clothed in the Rosh, down to the Malchut of Malchut, which is called Tabur; for then the Tabur becomes the concluding point. And the reason is that the first restriction was only upon the vessel of Malchut, which had already clothed the lights, as is known. (Inner Observation, Chapter 7, Item 3)
